subject.title: [Feature]: Add provider-profile routing policies for multi-account OAuth/API pools (starting with google-gemini-cli)

question: Should OpenClaw add a native provider-profile pool routing contract for batch/worker workloads, or keep the current bounded rotation/fallback model and solve only narrower provider-specific quota issues?
rationale: The request adds new auth/provider routing semantics, config surface, state accounting, and user-observable behavior across sessions and model fallback, which cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Keep as design umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/RFC owner and require any implementation to reuse one opt-in provider-pool contract instead of adding provider-specific ad hoc knobs.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Move only concrete bugs such as same-provider rotation or Gemini bucket cooldown into narrower issues and close this umbrella after maintainers decide there will be no general pool policy.

options.title: Decline native pool routing
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's current session-sticky/default rotation behavior and document external sidecars or plugins for explicit batch-pool orchestration.

recommendation.title: Keep as design umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/RFC owner and require any implementation to reuse one opt-in provider-pool contract instead of adding provider-specific ad hoc knobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the clearest current-code routing candidate from recent blame on the auth-profile ordering, failover, and config surfaces.
